notes: Event date: early May 1945, represented as 1 May (de Jong, Het Koninkrijk der Nederlanden in de Tweede Wereldoorlog, deel 10a, pp. 757-758). Event definition: A return compiled in London by the department of war gives, for early May 1945, two battalions of Bewakingstroepen and about 1,500 men. De Jong warns that this is too low (van Ojen has 13,000-14,000 at the end of December 1944 and about 16,000 in mid-January 1945), explains the drop by transfers into Koninklijke Landmacht components, the 19 gezagscompagnieën of early March (about 4,000 men), purges, and the London "two battalions" covering only companies already grouped in battalions, and tells the reader to take it that there were more than 10,000 Bewakingstroepen in the liberated south. This row uses de Jong's own working figure, not the London return he rejects. The London figures are recorded in the notes, not as a second claim or a conflict group, because they come from the same source family and de Jong is correcting his own cited return, not recording a disagreement between two sources. Location: Southern Netherlands (liberated area), existing place PL4153, precision 50 km.
